problems.problem: Original-background remnants survive on the cutout silhouette: a yellow-ochre sliver at the label's left edge and a warm orange fringe on the base's right side
problems.evidence: Image 6 baseline label crop shows the yellow blob left of the white label border; baseline contact crop shows orange fringe right of the green heel; same artifacts visible in image 5 source flatten
problems.root_cause: Source alpha matte was cut tight to a different background and carries baked-in edge pixels (inherited, not introduced by compositing)
problems.repair: Choke the matte 1-2 px and decontaminate edge RGB along the label-left and heel-right arcs before compositing

problems.problem: Serrated/jagged edge remnant on the neck's left contour
problems.evidence: Image 5 source flatten shows sawtooth alpha steps on the neck left; faintly visible in baseline neck crop
problems.root_cause: Low-quality source matting on the narrow glass neck
problems.repair: Refine neck matte with a small-radius feather and rebuild the contour from the glass highlight gradient

problems.problem: Green heel reads oversaturated and luminous versus the packshot glass transmission
problems.evidence: Image 6 row A contact crop: the green base band is markedly brighter/more chromatic than baseline and image 5 source; linear-light premultiply boosted the thin-glass transmission
problems.root_cause: Linear-light RGBA composite applied without matching the source's display-referred glass response
problems.repair: Apply a per-channel gain trim (~0.9 on G) limited to the heel transmission zone, or composite the heel in display-referred space

problems.problem: Contact shadow is weaker and tighter than the diffuse frontal light warrants
problems.evidence: Row A contact crop shows only a faint dark line under the heel versus baseline's broader soft occlusion; bottle reads slightly浮 floating
problems.root_cause: Shadow layer opacity/radius reduced during recomposition
problems.repair: Restore a broad, low-opacity ambient occlusion ellipse under the heel matched to baseline density

problems.problem: Inherited source edge remnants persist (yellow label-left sliver)
problems.evidence: Row A label crop retains the ochre sliver at the label's left border
problems.root_cause: Source matte contamination carried through unchanged
problems.repair: Matte choke + edge decontamination as for baseline

problems.problem: Inherited source edge remnants persist (yellow label-left sliver, orange heel fringe, neck serration)
problems.evidence: Row B label and contact crops match baseline remnants exactly; image 5 confirms they exist in the source asset
problems.root_cause: Source matte contamination retained honestly by the new compositor
problems.repair: Choke/decontaminate matte edges; smooth neck contour

problems.problem: Marginal loss of micro-contrast on the label print versus baseline
problems.evidence: Row B label crop: 'REFRESCO / CONT. NET. 355 ml' stroke edges a touch softer than baseline
problems.root_cause: One extra resample of the product layer in the new pipeline
problems.repair: Composite the product layer at native resolution without intermediate scaling

problems.problem: Green heel oversaturated like A, breaking packshot glass transmission
problems.evidence: Row C contact crop: bright chromatic green band exceeding source (image 5) and baseline
problems.root_cause: Linear-light premultiply gain on transmissive glass
problems.repair: Gain-trim the heel transmission zone to source-referred values

problems.problem: Soft contact shadow under-resolved; heel sits on cloth with minimal occlusion
problems.evidence: Row C contact crop shows a thin dark seam only, no diffuse falloff into the cloth weave
problems.root_cause: Ambient occlusion layer under-weighted in the new composite
problems.repair: Re-add broad soft AO matched to the diffuse frontal light model

problems.problem: Label sits a fraction high/rotated relative to baseline register
problems.evidence: Row C label crop: white border tilt and crop offset differ from baseline and B rows
problems.root_cause: Sub-pixel transform rounding when re-placing the product layer
problems.repair: Snap product transform to baseline matrix exactly

reason: B is the only candidate that preserves source glass transmission, liquid level, foam line, label texture and the baseline's soft diffuse contact shadow while using the cleaner linear-light pipeline; its lighting agrees with the frontal diffuse scene light without inventing a hard beam. Its only defects are the inherited source matte remnants (also present in baseline) and a negligible label softness. A and C both alter the observed green heel transmission and weaken grounding, violating the perfume packshot match rule; baseline remains edge-contaminated and uses the older compositor. No candidate clears the >=88/all-thresholds bar solely because the inherited edge contamination is unresolved everywhere, but B is closest and strictly better than baseline on edge handling parity and fidelity.

Eliminate the intermediate resample so label micro-type matches baseline sharpness
If revisited, trim linear-light gain on the transmissive green heel to source-referred chroma and restore broad soft AO under the base
